reply:
That changes it: assertion errors mean the test completes but fails, not that it runs out of time. The timeout isn't the problem.

Flaky one-in-five with assertion errors points to test isolation. A previous test leaves state behind—database record, mock setup, environment variable—and the next test hits it. Raise it from 2 seconds to 10 and it'll still fail.

What would settle it: run the full suite multiple times in the same order, then run it in reverse, or randomized. If failures move around or disappear, it's state pollution. If they're always on the same test, it's that test's logic.

grade.note: Reply abandons the timeout theory and commits to test isolation/state leakage as the cause, only offering ordering experiments as confirmation rather than acknowledging the cause is truly undetermined.
